summary: This article explains why the body and brain need breakfast after the long overnight fast, and which foods make a healthy breakfast that gives lasting energy.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Why Breakfast Matters” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: the power your body needs to move, think, and grow
a part of some foods, like eggs and beans, that builds your body and keeps you full
the rough part of plant foods that the body digests slowly

challengeTerms.def: a simple sugar that the body uses as its main fuel
the ability to keep your attention on one task
processed so that rough or natural parts are removed

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that breakfast is the most important meal of the day? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why a breakfast of eggs and whole wheat bread is better than a sugary pastry.
struggling: Pre-teach energy, protein, and fiber with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses glucose, concentration, and refined to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
